The fix is verified. Here's a summary of my work:

## Diagnosis

Both reported issues live in `IntroScreenActivity.java`, in the two slide fragments:

**Issue 1 — slide 3 showed the wrong encryption method.**
`AuthenticationFragment` had its `encryptionType` field hard-coded to `KEYSTORE`, and its layout hard-coded the description to `intro_slide3_desc_keystore`. The encryption slide defaults to *Password / PIN* and announces this through `onEncryptionChanged`, but that callback fires while `EncryptionFragment.onCreateView()` runs — at which point the auth fragment's view doesn't exist yet, so `updateEncryptionType()` hit its `if (desc != null)` guard and silently dropped the update. `onCreateView()` never re-applied the stored type, so the stale KeyStore text survived. Selecting KeyStore and going back re-triggered the callback *after* the view existed, which is exactly why the reporter saw it fix itself that way.

**Issue 2 — "authentication is optional" but a red "Please set a password" warning.**
The auth method was unconditionally initialized to `PASSWORD`, regardless of the encryption type, so choosing KeyStore left a blocking password requirement that contradicted the on-screen text.

I also found a latent defect: both fragments derived their state from the spinner widgets and re-forced `PASSWORD` on every `onCreateView()`, so a user's choice was silently discarded whenever the ViewPager recreated a slide's view.

## The fix

- Both fragments now keep their selection in a **field that is the source of truth** and re-apply it in `onCreateView()`, so state survives view recreation and no longer depends on fragment creation order.
- Added `defaultAuthMethod(encryptionType)`: `PASSWORD` encryption → `PASSWORD` auth (required), `KEYSTORE` → `NONE` (optional), matching what the slide text promises.
- `updateEncryptionType()` now ignores redundant notifications, updates the description via a shared `updateViews()`, and adjusts the auth method to the new encryption type's default only when the type actually changes.
- Aligned the two layouts' placeholder texts with the real default, and added null-guards in `canGoForward()`.

## Verification

Gradle couldn't run — this environment has no network at all and Android Gradle Plugin 3.1.3 isn't in the local cache (`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` fails on dependency download, before any of my changes are even reached). I verified compilation directly instead:

- Built a classpath from the cached AARs/JARs plus `android-28.jar`, generated stub `R`/`BuildConfig` classes, and compiled `IntroScreenActivity.java` with `javac` using sourcepath resolution — **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- Compiled both modified layouts with `aapt2` — both succeed, confirming the string references resolve.

Two unrelated errors appear if I force-compile `MainActivity`/`AboutActivity` in that ad-hoc setup; they come from AndroidX-based libraries (speed-dial, aboutlibraries) that Gradle's jetifier rewrites at build time. Those files are untouched by this patch.

I traced the reported reproduction steps through the new code: the default flow now shows the Password/PIN text on slide 3, selecting KeyStore switches the auth method to *None* with no red warning, and switching back to Password/PIN restores the required-password behaviour.
